report.answer: A yellow tennis ball is thrown across a room in a clean projectile arc, then sticks the landing. Flight fits projectile-with-drag with g ~10.0 m/s2 and launch ~6.0 m/s, matching Earth gravity. After hitting the floor around frame 32 it is essentially at rest at ~2 mm/s — a dead, no-bounce inelastic impact.
assumptions: motion roughly in a plane facing the camera
tennis-ball diameter 0.067 m at same depth as motion sets scale

forks.label: vacuum flight
forks.why: show same arc without drag: slightly farther and faster impact

forks.label: Moon throw
forks.why: same 6 m/s throw floats ~6x longer and farther under lunar g

forks.label: bouncy ball
forks.why: replace dead impact with lively tennis bounce to contrast energy loss
